title: Column generation in one worked example

questions.heading: Stop When No Day Has a Negative Reduced Cost; the Pricing Value Bounds the LP on the Way
questions.stem: Mid-run, a crew-day restricted master LP stands at 50.4 days, and the pricing problem's best day is worth 1.2 days of work at the current prices. What does this say about the full master LP's optimum?

options.text: It lies between 42.0 and 50.4, as 50.4 / 1.2 = 42.0 bounds it from below
options.says: Right: the scaled prices are dual feasible for the full LP, so z_RMP / v* is a lower bound, and z_RMP an upper one.

options.text: It lies between 49.2 and 50.4, as 50.4 - 1.2 = 49.2 bounds it from below
options.says: The bound divides by the pricing value; subtracting it has no basis.

options.text: It lies at 50.4, as the restricted master's value is already the LP's value
options.says: A day with reduced cost 1 - 1.2 = -0.2 exists, so adding it can still lower the LP.

options.text: It lies between 50.4 and 60.5, as 50.4 x 1.2 = 60.5 bounds it from above
options.says: The restricted master's value is an upper bound on the full LP, which has more columns; 60.5 bounds nothing.

questions.heading: Integer Answers Come From the Generated Columns, and the LP Bound Says How Good They Are
questions.stem: Column generation ends with a master LP optimum of 61.2 crew-days, and the integer master over the generated columns uses 63. What can be reported?

options.text: The best plan uses 62 or 63 days; 63 is in hand and 62 is not ruled out
options.says: Right: the LP proves at least 62 whole days; price-and-branch found 63 and cannot prove more.

options.text: The best plan uses 63 days; the integer master over the columns is exact
options.says: The best plan may need a column the LP never priced; the page calls price-and-branch a heuristic with a bound.

options.text: The best plan uses 62 days; the LP optimum rounded up is reached by it
options.says: Rounding up gives a bound; whether a 62-day plan exists is open without branch-and-price.

options.text: The best plan uses 61.2 days; a fraction of a day is worked as part of a day
options.says: Crew-days are whole; the LP's fractional days are a relaxation, not a plan.

questions.heading: A Compact Model of the Same Question Checks the Answer and Shows Why Patterns Help
questions.stem: A planner builds the compact model of a crew-day season (a count per task kind and day, a yes/no per day) and finds its LP bound almost a day below the pattern LP's. Why?

options.text: The compact LP leaves out the 600-minute limit on the tasks of each day
options.says: The compact model has a 600-minute row per day (day_k on the page); what it allows is splitting a task, not overfilling a day.

options.text: The compact LP lets the minutes of one task run across two separate days
options.says: Right: every pattern is a whole day that fits, so the pattern LP cannot split a task; the compact LP can.

options.text: The pattern LP rounds each day's count up, so its bound adds the rounding
options.says: The pattern LP's day counts are continuous; nothing is rounded in it.

options.text: The pattern LP was stopped early, so its value sits above its own optimum
options.says: Stopped at convergence, as on the page, the pattern LP's value is its optimum, and it still exceeds the compact LP's.
